cohort: The study included singleton adolescent pregnant women with a pre-pregnancy self-reported BMI of 18.5-29.9, recruited during their first-trimester visit over five years.
finding: Overweight adolescent pregnant women experienced significantly higher rates of adverse obstetrical outcomes and neonatal complications compared to their appropriate-weight counterparts.
mod_finding: Primary Cesarean section was significantly higher in overweight adolescent pregnant women with an odds ratio of 1.5 (95% CI: 1.06-2.2).
